irreducible_signature.reason: Both remove answer_mode, focus role/type, subject type, and deixis. V26.2 also expresses evidence claims once by construction.

tagged_proof.reason: V26.2 requires an evidence object with relation/subject/time, each a closed tagged union. V25.3.1 uses parallel kind/id fields and canonicalizes anchors.

unicode_segmentation.reason: Both use the same frozen Unicode UAX #29 segmenter; ZH=4 and JA=9 in mutation tests.

surface_contamination.reason: V26.2 formal audit reports zero source/mixed lines, zero whole queries, and zero n-gram overlap >=3 on 109+34+70.

semantic_retry.reason: V26.2 makes exactly one call. V25.3.1 retains a second attempt path.

validator_authority.reason: V26.2 validates only schema, ids, spans, and proof references; it never changes semantic claims or routes. V25.3.1 canonicalizes proof anchors.

not_evaluated_accounting.reason: Transport/schema/span failures are NOT_EVALUATED; ambiguous is excluded. Binding, signature, and evaluable gates are separate.

gold_isolation.reason: V26.2 freezes an AST isolation check and uses opaque fixture ids; request_body/call_once/run_case cannot access fixture/gold symbols.

known_risks: Every evidence tagged union keeps the none branch first; prior experiments showed branch-order/default collapse is possible. The native run must report evidence completeness separately.

Unsupported records remain binding-evaluable while ambiguous records are NOT_EVALUATED. This cannot hide failure from the required 34/34 signature-exact gate, but future reports should expose unsupported_count separately.
The tagged schema is larger than the V25.3.1 flat schema; live latency and grammar-compiler behavior remain unproven.
The 34/34 V25.3 post-hoc rescore proves signal only; it gives no acceptance credit to V26.2.
